title: Nvidia's Blowout Quarter Just Made These Stocks Massive Winners
summary: Couch Investor recaps Nvidia's blowout quarter (stock +6%): revenue +106% YoY with ~90% growth guided, Q3 revenue guided to $108B, gross margin 75% easing to ~74% then a 71.5% trough before recovering to 72.5% in FY28 on extreme memory pricing. The bombshell: FY28 revenue growth guided to ~70% — far above expectations, ~100% if unconstrained. Data center grew 117%, with the neocloud segment (ACI) up 138% and nearing half of data center revenue; AWS will deploy 2M additional GPUs ($200B potential revenue); Vera Rubin shipments began in early August as the fastest product ramp ever (30x throughput/MW, 35x lower token cost); networking up 18% QoQ with Spectrum-X up 2.6x YoY; Grok LPX systems shipping with Nebius first. Management signaled ~$1.3-1.4T of 2027 capex (bad for hyperscaler free cash flow, great for semis/neoclouds), $366B in balance-sheet commitments ($279B supply/capacity, primarily memory), ~$50B in frontier-lab investments, and $500B+ third-party financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman, and KKR. His updated DCF gives a $309 probability-weighted price — +38.7% upside. He then maps the beneficiaries: memory (SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung), foundry/packaging (TSMC, Amkor, Teradyne), networking (Astera Labs, Credo, Coherent, Lumentum, Marvell, Arista, Amphenol), power/cooling (Vertiv, nVent, GE Vernova), neoclouds (Nebius, CoreWeave, Equinix), system builders (Dell, Supermicro, HPE, Celestica), and Arm — with AMD picking up spillover demand, while noting some names already price in much success. Call: NVDA BUY.
